name: Downtown and Roosevelt Row
tagline: Murals, coffee bars and the only truly walkable Phoenix grid
description: Roosevelt Row is a stretch of galleries, muralled walls, coffee bars and low rise bungalows immediately north of the downtown towers and ASU's downtown campus. It is the one part of Phoenix where you can live without a car, with the Valley Metro light rail running along Central Avenue.
bestFor: Nomads who want to skip the rental car and work from cafes and co-working floors.
pros: Light rail on Central Avenue reaches Tempe and the airport
Highest density of cafes and co-working desks in the metro
First Friday art walk and a real events calendar
cons: Summer heat above 110F makes midday walking unsafe
Sports and concert nights bring traffic and noise
Visible homelessness on some downtown blocks

name: Melrose and Midtown
tagline: Seventh Avenue vintage shops and cheap central bungalows
description: The Melrose District on 7th Avenue is neon signs, vintage furniture stores, dive bars and a long standing LGBTQ scene, backed by streets of 1940s and 50s ranch bungalows. Midtown just east adds office towers, the Heard Museum and light rail. Rents sit well below Arcadia or Scottsdale for a similarly central spot.
bestFor: Longer stay nomads who want a central address without downtown or Scottsdale prices.
pros: Good value rents for a central location
Light rail along Central Avenue into downtown
Character bungalows with yards and mature trees
cons: 7th Avenue traffic is fast and noisy
Still car dependent for most grocery runs
Quality varies block to block, walk it first

name: Arcadia
description: Arcadia is old citrus grove land turned into large ranch lots with irrigated lawns and grapefruit trees, sitting directly under Camelback Mountain. The 40th Street and Indian School corridors hold the coffee shops and restaurants. It is green, quiet and clearly the metro's most desirable residential pocket.
bestFor: Nomads with a budget who want hiking trails and lawns instead of concrete.
pros: Camelback and Piestewa trailheads within minutes
Genuinely green and shaded compared with the rest of the city
Strong local restaurant and coffee cluster
cons: Expensive, among the highest rents in the metro
No light rail, driving is mandatory
Camelback trail parking overflows all winter

name: Old Town Scottsdale
tagline: Resort pools, galleries and a dense nightlife grid
description: Old Town Scottsdale packs galleries, western storefronts, restaurants and a large nightlife district into a compact walkable grid, wrapped in resorts and newer apartment blocks. The Scottsdale Waterfront and the paved Arizona Canal path run through it. It draws the highest concentration of visitors and short stay renters in the metro.
bestFor: Nomads who want resort amenities, pools and a walkable nightlife scene.
pros: Compact and walkable by Phoenix standards
Excellent gyms, pools and short term furnished rentals
Canal path gives a flat cycling and running route
cons: Expensive, and rates spike during spring training
Loud bar district on weekend nights
No light rail connection, a car or rideshare is needed

name: Tempe and Mill Avenue
tagline: ASU campus energy beside a lake and a light rail line
description: Tempe wraps around Arizona State University, with Mill Avenue as its bar and cafe spine and Tempe Town Lake providing a rare stretch of water and paths. Papago Park and A Mountain sit at the edges. Student density means cheap sublets, plenty of gyms and the best bike infrastructure in the metro.
bestFor: Nomads who want bikeable streets, cheap sublets and constant campus buzz.
pros: Best cycling network and bike lanes in the metro
Light rail straight into downtown Phoenix
Cheap furnished student sublets, especially in summer
cons: Very loud around Mill Avenue during term time
Summer heat plus lake humidity is punishing
Rentals turn over on the academic calendar, not yours
